name: AstroAsk
tagline: An AI chat that reads your natal chart and answers questions about it.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Two things are happening here: an ephemeris calculation and a language model with a personality. The first is a solved problem with free, accurate open source libraries that have been correct since before the web existed. The second is a system prompt and an API key. There is no shared data, no network, nothing you get from other users' charts, so a personal build keeps essentially the whole value as long as you are willing to pay per token and live without a polished mobile app.
coreLoopDIY: Takes your birth date, time and place, computes a real natal chart with planetary positions, houses and aspects, then feeds that chart into an LLM as structured context so you can chat with it about your placements.
requirements: An LLM API key (or a local model if you want zero per-token cost)
A geocoding source or a hardcoded lat/long/timezone for your birth city
A Swiss Ephemeris binding or equivalent astronomy library
Node 20+ and a browser; runs on localhost
whatYouLose: A real mobile app with push notifications for daily transits
A tone that has been tuned over thousands of conversations instead of your first draft of a system prompt
Handling for the annoying edge cases: unknown birth times, historical timezone changes, house system disputes
Synastry, composite and multi-person features unless you build them yourself
Someone else eating the inference bill and the hallucination complaints
moatNotes: Astrology apps live or die on voice and vibe, which is a real skill, just not a technical moat.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because most of the audience wants an app on their phone that feels like a person, not a localhost tab with a text box. The chart math is free and public, the interpretation is a prompt, but the product is the feeling of being read accurately by something warm at 1am, and that comes from copy, pacing and design choices that a one-shot build will approximate rather than match. Also, nobody who buys this wants to think about API keys.
notes: The hard part was solved by 16th century astronomers and shipped as an MIT-licensed library; everything after that is tone of voice.
prompt:
Build a local-only natal chart chat app called "chartchat" in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 14 App Router with TypeScript and Tailwind
- better-sqlite3 for local persistence in ./data/chartchat.db
- the "sweph" npm package (Swiss Ephemeris bindings) for planetary positions
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions via fetch, base URL and model from .env

What it does:
1. On first run, an onboarding form: birth date, birth time (with an "unknown time" checkbox), and birth latitude, longitude and IANA timezone. No geocoding service; provide a small hardcoded list of about 40 major cities plus manual lat/long entry.
2. Compute a natal chart: Sun through Pluto plus Chiron, North Node, Ascendant and Midheaven, using Placidus houses and tropical zodiac. Compute major aspects (conjunction, opposition, square, trine, sextile) with configurable orbs, default 6 degrees for luminaries and 4 otherwise. If time is unknown, skip houses, Ascendant and Midheaven and label the chart "time unknown".
3. Render the chart as a clean table plus a simple SVG wheel. No canvas libraries, hand-roll the SVG.
4. A chat page. Every request sends a compact JSON summary of the chart as a system message alongside a system prompt that says: you are a knowledgeable astrologer, cite the specific placements you are reasoning from, never make medical, legal or financial predictions, and say when the chart does not support an answer. Stream the response.
5. Persist the chart and full chat history in SQLite. Allow multiple saved charts and switching between them.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, hosting, telemetry, payments, transits, progressions, synastry, push notifications, mobile apps.

Rules:
- Secrets only in .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_MODEL). Include .env.example and gitignore .env and ./data.
- Include a unit test asserting the chart engine returns known positions for a fixed reference datetime, so ephemeris wiring errors surface immediately.
- README with exact setup commands and one honest paragraph on house system choice and orb defaults being conventions, not truth.
- Ship it running with `npm run dev` on first try.
